plan_a_advantages: Includes a dedicated hill session for trail-specific power development.
Features a longer, controlled long run to build aerobic endurance.
More directly addresses the need for climbing strength, a key component of trail running.
plan_b_advantages: Incorporates a tempo run, which can be beneficial for speed work.
Includes a strength session focused on leg muscles, which is a good foundation for any running program.
reasoning: For a trail runner aiming to become faster, Plan A is the superior choice. It strategically incorporates threshold-paced hill work and a longer, dedicated long run – both crucial for developing the power and endurance needed for trail speed. Plan B, while including a tempo run, lacks the focused climbing work and longer sustained effort that directly translates to trail performance. Plan A’s structure prioritizes building the specific physiological adaptations required for trail running, while Plan B feels more generalized and less targeted towards the demands of the sport.
